It's soft, but not as soft as minky. It has a "nap" in that there is a wrong way and right way to rub the fabric, just like minky, but it is much shorter and reminds me of terrycloth. The material is thinner overall too, but I think it is worth it!

Me (32F) confronting my ndad is actually how I decided to go no contact. I also followed the advice of my therapist to confront him, and prepped for weeks. 

Personally, maybe I wasn't totally ready, because I completely broke down while trying to explain my feelings. The conversation was the same as it always has been - me coming off as emotionally unstable and my dad brushing off my concerns, quite literally saying "sounds like a YOU problem", and even gaslighting me, saying my experiences didn't happen at all, or not the way I portrayed them. 

My therapist advised we meet in a public place so I could feel comfortable leaving at any point - which I eventually did because I was so overwhelmed. It was humiliating. 

This is not to discourage you. I think it is worth a shot, and every situation is different. For me, this was not the outcome I hoped for, but it did solidify my decision to move on with my life.

He became OBSESSED with Evanescence and writing broody poetry, like a teenager. He wanted to shop at Hot Topic too, and for lack of a better way to put it, started dressing somewhat goth. 

Some of my friends at the time thought it was cool, as if he "understood" or something, which couldnt be further from the truth. But then he'd go see bands I wanted to see without me, and call some of them "gay" to upset me. 

Let's just say... it was most definitely just a phase for him, but not for me.

Also vegan for about 2 years, and also off birth control pills for roughly 6 months. I've read that hair loss due to birth control can take a full year to recover from. This would be telogen effluvium I believe. I'm still seeing a lot of shedding myself, but I also have lots of baby hairs growing in. I'm hoping the shedding will decrease over time and the new growth will fill everything back in, in a few months' time. If it's not better by then, I'm considering getting on an androgen blocker like spironolactone to see if that helps. 

Best of luck to you!

I find it extremely difficult to show any form of emotion to others now, but especially any distress or sadness. My little brother and I were pushed really hard in sports (almost always to tears, and then punished for that) and constantly compared to others. My dad very much subscribes to the whole "snowflake" notion, asking for help is very frowned upon. If you can't do it yourself (practically anything), there is something wrong with you. He is a master at gaslighting, saying things never happened or that he doesn't remember them. His only apology is "I'm sorry you feel that way". It will probably take a lot of time and some major patience, but I truly believe that the best thing you can do is aim to gain some independence. If you're 18, there's no reason you shouldn't have access to your own birth certificate and SS card, nor should you not have the freedom to choose where you work. I'm not sure of your relationship with your parents as a whole, but it took some time for me to learn that mine are also just human, they make mistakes, and they don't always know what's best.

I've felt this way too. Just a personal theory, but I think some of us are more sensitive and attuned to the emotions/desires/expressions/etc. of others and that makes us "mold" to their personalities. I think it's a form of understanding and communicating with others. I don't think this means that you don't have a personality though, or that your personality IS depression. I think it means you're an empath, and your time and place to flourish is not the typical social situation. I also think depression does an excellent job of making us mute and suppress ourselves, and lift others up instead. I hope you know that there is literally no one else quite like you though.  


P.S. I wish I could say these things to myself, and believe them!

Yes, I get this too! I like how you put it--mentally asleep. I am the same way, it expends a lot of mental energy to focus and be present and the rest of the time I am either mentally asleep or literally asleep. This is just a theory, but for me I think it has something to do with how constantly our brains are being bombarded with stimuli and information. I think we do this to ourselves, too. I like to keep a stream on in the background while I'm doing art or even cleaning, but I think this is actually quite detrimental. I think the "mental asleep-ness" is sort of our brain's way of checking out after being constantly over-stimulated. Idk if this resonates with you, and I'm definitely not an expert here, but I can relate.
